solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old brown sherry will corrupt fish, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the two words before are read backwards

parts.note: to corrupt is to rot
the cod is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: A drinker warns that an old sherry will spoil the fish course when you think about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records this word as an old name for a brown sherry used for blending.

clue.text: Most sober dissent is coming from Paris

parts.note: to demur is to raise an objection or dissent
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The most restrained disagreement, we are told, comes from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Demure means modest and serious, so its superlative is the most sober or staid.

clue.text: Rich satin fashioned for popstar Aguilera

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped or made into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A designer makes a rich satin outfit for a famous American singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina Aguilera is the American pop singer known for Genie in a Bottle.

clue.text: Apparently quiet god

parts.note: split as ..., the word reads as zero noise, which is apparently quiet

explanation.surface: A deity who seems to say very little.
explanation.walkthrough: O is nought and DIN is noise, so nought noise is quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Sensible case for brewing true wine

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the word for sensible surrounds the other letters

parts.note: sane means sensible or rational

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A practical box for making honest wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' looks like a container noun, and 'brewing' like a description of winemaking, but both are just signals here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region, also spelt Sauternes.

clue.text: Attribute good character to a church leader

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so this takes the opening letter of the word church

parts.note: credit is a good reputation or standing

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for the good name of a minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' places A and the church's first letter before CREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit or ascribe something to someone; accredit is used in the sense of attributing a saying or act.

clue.text: Fees involved with errant one being moved?

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Charges incurred alongside a stray person relocating.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing transferred to another place or owner is the recipient of a transfer.

clue.text: German poet may show anger about ending of limerick

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb for anger goes round the other letter

parts.note: to rile is to anger or annoy

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A German writer of verse gets cross at how a comic poem ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts K, the final letter of limerick, inside RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke wrote the Duino Elegies, in German, though he was born in Prague.

clue.text: Served up Greek wine, but not in European festival

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means sent upwards, so the word is read backwards
but not says the following word is left out

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: A Greek wine is poured at a festival across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes IN from RETSINA, leaving RETSA, and 'Served up' turns that into ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast celebrating the Resurrection is a major religious festival.

clue.text: Drink police presented to royalty

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Detectives offer the royal family a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: This alcoholic beverage is made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: Cocktail taken in one swallow for starters

parts.note: the house martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cocktail downed in a single gulp as an aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth mix is one of the best-known cocktails.

clue.text: Somewhat rich, a blissful Burgundy

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wine reviewer calls a Burgundy rich and rather heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from the northern part of the Burgundy region.

clue.text: Written work, page missing on table wine

indicators.note: missing means the letter for page is left out

parts.note: prose is ordinary written work, as opposed to verse

explanation.surface: A manuscript lies on the dining table with a leaf gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link here; the definition is 'table wine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosé is a pink wine commonly drunk with meals.

clue.text: Liquor in safe? Teachers demand

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a teacher writing on homework demands that the pupil come and see them

explanation.surface: Drink hidden in the strongbox is what the staff insist on.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is old thieves' slang; 'See me' is the note a teacher writes on poor work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedro Ximénez, anglicised as Peter-see-me, is a sweet Spanish wine and the grape it comes from.

clue.text: Documentation making office assistant get saucy and protest

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
pert means cheeky or saucy
to rail is to complain or protest vehemently

explanation.surface: A secretary becomes cheeky and complains, prompting written records.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail of documents records a series of transactions, so it is a body of documentation.

clue.text: A red blouse shortened, taken to literal extremes

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a blouse is a type of shirt
the extremes of the alphabet, the literal letters, are its first and last, A and Z

explanation.surface: A red top is cropped and treated too literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literal' here means to do with letters, so its extremes are A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: This red grape variety, also called Syrah, gives a red wine.

clue.text: Poor Cressida dropped small cocktail

indicators.note: poor means badly formed, so these letters are rearranged
dropped says the letter for small is removed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Cressida lets fall a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes one S from CRESSIDA, and 'Poor' rearranges the rest, CREIDA plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: This cocktail mixes brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Fun as a goddess intended?

definitions.meaning: split as A MUSE MEANT, it says a goddess of the arts intended something

explanation.surface: Enjoyment is what the goddess had in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading: one of the nine Muses meant it.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment and enjoyment are both straightforward synonyms of fun.

clue.text: Arrive casually, light wind having gathered?

parts.note: a breeze is a gentle or light wind
crops that have been gathered are in, brought in from the fields

explanation.surface: Someone drifts in as a gentle wind picks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is only a link joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to stroll in relaxed and unannounced.

clue.text: Worries about the birds' protection

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for worries goes round the article

parts.note: fears are worries or anxieties

explanation.surface: Concerns over how birds are kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage keeps birds warm and dry, so it serves as their protective covering.

clue.text: Cheese being rejected, Gershwin produced wine

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese
Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

explanation.surface: After his cheese was turned away, the lyricist made wine instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This fortified wine comes from a Portuguese island in the Atlantic.

clue.text: Old airline with a French wine

parts.note: BEA was British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974
une is French for a

explanation.surface: A former carrier serving a French vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a town in Burgundy that names a red wine of the Côte d'Or.

clue.text: Scratch player or statistician?

definitions.meaning: one who scratches or cuts marks into a surface
the person who keeps the tally of points or runs in a game

explanation.surface: Is that golfer with no handicap really the one keeping the numbers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch player' suggests a golfer with no handicap, but here it means someone who scratches.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are agent nouns: one who marks lines, and one who records points in a match.

clue.text: Sort of tea service aristocrats initially rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Nobles turning down a tea service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses MASSA, MASS plus A from 'aristocrats initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: This black tea comes from a state in north-east India with the same name.

clue.text: Liqueur exemplified by environmentally friendly map- readers?

definitions.meaning: a herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks
map-readers who are green would ..., using their maps again

explanation.surface: A liqueur typifies eco-minded navigators.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CHART REUSE: a chart is a map, and reuse is the green habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French liqueur made by monks of the Grande Chartreuse also names a yellow-green colour.

clue.text: Saw girl, huge, being cut in half

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: cut in half keeps only the back half of the word

explanation.surface: A very large girl is sawn in two, like a magician's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut in half' leaves GE, the second half of 'huge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, the same as a maxim.

clue.text: Arranged shock treatment — no Montrachet — another wine

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
no says the letters of the second word are taken away from the first group

explanation.surface: A wine buff is given shock therapy, with no Burgundy allowed, only a different wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of MONTRACHET from SHOCK TREATMENT: S, K, E and T remain to be arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sekt is German sparkling wine.

clue.text: Article detailed Thailand and its location

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its tail cut off, losing the last letter

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A report sets out Thailand and where it lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its location' refers back to Thailand: the continent where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand lies in South-East Asia, so the continent is where it is located.

clue.text: All are drunk on English beer

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and muddled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Everyone is tipsy on English ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned beer, championed by CAMRA in Britain, goes by this name.

clue.text: A custom imbibing the French and choice German wine

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the word for custom takes the other letters inside

parts.note: use means habit or custom
les is French for the, in the plural

explanation.surface: A habit of drinking French and fine German wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Auslese means selection in German and labels wine made from selected, very ripe bunches.

clue.text: Chips topped with fish and white wine

indicators.note: topped means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: fries are chips, as in French fries
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Fish and chips washed down with a white.
explanation.definitionFit: This German grape gives a well-known white wine.

clue.text: While in training is given alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in says the word for while sits inside the letters for training

parts.note: PT is physical training
as means while, at the time that

explanation.surface: An athlete in training is handed a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured spirit from the south of France.
